recipes.name: Jill's Hash Brown Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can Campbell's® Condensed Cream of Mushroom Soup (Regular, 98% Fat Free or 25% Less Sodium)

steps.text: Mix soup, sour cream, butter, potatoes, onion, cheese and black pepper to taste in 3-quart shallow baking dish. Sprinkle corn flakes over potato mixture.
Bake at 350 degrees F for 45 minutes or until hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Jill's Hash Brown Casserole
raw_recipe.description: Perfect as a side dish for brunch or dinner, this creamy and crunchy hash brown casserole always fits the bill.

review.reviewBody:
This is even better with crumbled crisp
bacon or cooked breakfast sausage. I add in a cup of shredded cheddar or swiss.
You can substitute plain yogurt if you don't have sour cream. TIP: This is great
if you make this the night before and take it out 15 minutes before you stick it in the oven. I usually serve this with
english muffin bread or big fluffy biscuits.

I made this last night for dinner but I had to find the calorie count since I am only eating a certain amount of things. But my son loved it so much that he wants it for Christmas too. And I cooked it for an hour covered and some of the potatoes still were not cooked all the way through.. 
 
I made a few changes see below which made the individual serving only 315 calories per serving. 

1 can (10 1/2 ounces) Kroger Condensed Cream of Mushroom Soup 
8 ounces (1 container) sour cream 
1/2 bag (32 ounces) frozen hash brown potatoes (about 15 oz) 
6 oz of cooked chicken breast strips
1 6 oz of green giant mexicorn
2 tbsp real bacon bits
1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese (about 4 ounces) 
1/8 teaspoon ground black pepper 
4 tbsp bread crumbs

I swapped out cream of mushroom for cream of chicken, added 8oz chopped up andouille, cut the cheese in half, reduced the butter to 1/4 cup, half an onion diced , 3 cloves of garlic minced, 2 peppers sliced,and used fat free 6oz of sour cream. I'd give it a 9/10 :) The sausage provided the fat I had taken out by reducing the butter. Pretty solid main dish (think hot dish with a twist).

This was AWESOME!! I made it for my Mother's Day brunch, and everyone raved about it! The only changes I made were due to the fact that I didn't have 2 of the exact ingredients the recipe called for. The first was the soup. I used cream of chicken and mushroom soup. DELICIOUS!! The second was the topping. I didn't have cornflakes, so I mixed panko bread crumbs with a little melted butter and spread thet over the top. It made a nice crispy, golden topping. I would do it again that way. One other suggestion I would make would be to thoroughly defrost the hash browns. I've made similar casseroles in the past and have learned that the hash browns cook much better if they have been defrosted first. This is by far my favorite hash brown casserole recipe. You gotta try it!

my mother in-law has been making this for years for our Christmas morning breakfast at my house. I started making it using this recipe. it is so good. I use cream of chicken as my mom is allergic to mushroom and use a bigger pan and more cornflakes add a sprinkle of garlic and onion powder. not big changes. making it right now for my mom and I for mothers day. thanks for sharing.

Turned out great in the slow cooker. I omitted the sour cream , mixed cheddar and mozzarella cheese, and used bread crumbs instead of corn flakes. Everything worked well together and tasted great for brunch

Great recipe. After reading other reviews, I was unsure about using cream of chicken or cream of mushroom, but Campbell's makes a cream of chicken & mushroom that worked perfectly. I got rave reviews. I used italian bread crumbs instead of corn flakes.The only thing I will do differently next time is sautee the onions before mixing it all together so they're a little more tender.

Very easy and whole family liked it. To make into a main course, I add a pound of cooked ground beef and a sprinkle of garlic powder. About 5 minutes before it is finished, I top with a can of French fried onions instead of the corn flakes.

I baked this casserole for 45 minutes according to the instructions, but the hashbrowns (used frozen as directed) were not fully cooked and a little crunchy, so after dinner I put it back in the oven for another 30 minutes and that took care of it. 
I thought this recipe was a little bland and could have used a little salt. We did not care for the cornflakes on top because we found them to be chewy after they were cooked. I would try an alternative topping, like bread crumbs or ritz crackers mixed with a little butter. Speaking of butter, I think you could easily half the amount of butter and it would be better and less greasy. 
I probably wouldn't make this again if my husband hadn't loved it so much. I will make the changes above and try it again since he seemed to really like the idea of this casserole.

This is delicious! Sometimes I use cream of chicken soup instead of mushroom but both are great! I fry the onion first before adding it and I always add a bit more than a cup of cheese to the mixture. The topping is important to me... I sprinkle parm cheese over the casserole then mix 3 tbsp of melted butter with the crushed corn flakes. It makes the casserole nice and crispy and there's really no substitute for corn flakes. Nothing else is quite as good!!!
Doesn’t need the cornflakes and if you use O’Brien hash browns you can omit adding the onion.
If you find that the potatoes are harder than you would like after baking, I prefer to thaw my potatoes in the refrigerator over night. This helps the cooking process of the potatoes.

Family favorite for sure.. I've added real bacon pieces, I've also made it with some of flakes of ham. I always add more shredded cheese, it's a must!! Next I'll be making it with adding a can of corn!! So many possibilities.
This is a really easy, good tasting recipe. I made this for my church potluck, so I increased the recipe and added sausage. I also used Cream of Chicken instead of Mushroom soup. It was a big hit.
Only changeI made was to mix dried fried onionswith the corn flakes as a topping. It was a hit.

We love this version of potato casserole. We have a few members of our family that do not eat meat, so the other recipes that call for cream of chicken soup don't work for us. I follow this recipe to a T and it is always delicious. Sometimes we top with crushed crackers or just top with a little cheese and bread crumbs if we don't have corn flakes in our house. We love it really hot, so we bake for more time, but that is just personal to each cook and how their oven works. Great recipe!
I've been making this for years. The one thing that makes it taste a lot better in my opinion is to cook the onions in butter first. I microwave them.

I had this at Cracker Barrel and had to try and make it for myself. This makes a lot and is hard to for a single person to use up. I’ll make it again, but will try to cut things in half. You can’t go wrong on taste here.
I followed the recipe exactly and baked it for 45 minutes. The potatoes were still hard. Will not use this recipe again.
Great recipe! I may add sausage or ham to it next time I make it.
